Live Claude sessions

Live Claude CLI sessions per client conversation: when they continue, reseed or fall back.

About 19 min read · 10 sections

On this page
01 How a request is served 02 Reasoning-summary replay 03 Admission 04 Prompt cache across threads 05 Safety 06 Request rejections 07 Authentication failures 08 Context management 09 Measured 10 Restarts and upgrades

By default (claudeSessions.mode: "live"), the gateway keeps one stream-json CLI process per identified client conversation, the way Claude Code itself runs. Codex thread IDs and native Claude Code session metadata identify their own conversations. Session-only clients have a separate internal namespace; an arbitrary user ID never groups chats. The CLI holds the native history: real tool_use and tool_result turns, signed thinking that carries across tool steps, and a prompt cache that grows by appending.

{ "id": "claude", "type": "claude-subscription", "claudeSessions": { "mode": "live" } }

The daemon reads the change on its next request. Explicit "replay" turns it off; running sessions finish their turn and close. A provider in replay mode retires its own parked sessions on its next request, so they do not wait out the park timer. Retirement also tracks CLIs still initializing. Their already-accepted request finishes normally, then the session closes instead of remaining parked in replay mode.

Setting Default Meaning
mode live live keeps a session per conversation; explicit replay uses standalone requests
max 10% of RAM Live sessions in the whole process. An explicit positive safe integer has no fixed upper ceiling; use 64 to double a 32-slot pool. The default remains clamp(floor(0.10 × totalmem / 300 MB), 6, 32): 6 up to 20 GiB, 21 on 64 GiB, 32 from about 94 GiB. A session being started counts toward it
parkMinutes 60 Idle time before a session closes (5–240), per session
warmup 1 Completed requests a thread needs before its first live session may start (0–5). 0 restores immediate spawning.
replayFormat text Item encoding for one-shot requests and session seeds; json restores the old one

How a request is served

  • Continue: the request carries the history the session already has plus new items. Tool outputs go back to the CLI's waiting MCP calls through a private relay (a 0600 Unix socket with a per-session key). The relay carries only the RPC id, the tool name and the tool_use id, never arguments. A new user turn is sent as one message.

  • Reseed (a new process, one cache write): the model, thinking, Fast, system prompt, tool catalog or window changed (fingerprint_changed, window_changed), or the session was idle 60 minutes or more (idle_expired; see Context management below). A fingerprint_changed reseed records which part changed as changed (model, thinking, fast, instructions, tools), with tool counts only; see diagnostics. The tool catalog is already sorted by name with canonical schemas, so reordering alone never reseeds. The cache of the old session is gone or unusable either way, so the new process costs no more than the next one-shot request would.

  • Messages after tools: when every pending tool result is followed by new user or developer messages, the gateway queues only those new messages on the existing CLI. An empty-settings control acknowledgment orders that input before Gateway releases the waiting MCP results. This acknowledgment does not start another inference. Caller roles remain in the rendered message blocks. The messages may also come before or between the results: Codex records a message sent while a tool runs (a steer) where it arrived, which is before the tool's output, and a subagent's report after it. Every pending result must still appear exactly once, the tail must cover the rest of the conversation, and only those caller messages render, after the results; tool results never render as text. On 2026-11-03 a chat waiting on wait_agent got both and was refused as unexpected_tail until its session expired an hour later. Missing or duplicate tool results, a new call, edited prefixes and appended assistant output keep their existing checks. Older adopted instances without queued-input support reseed once through messages_after_tools. A rejected or timed-out acknowledgment, cancellation during the handoff, or CLI/relay failure during the steered request closes the unsafe session and ends the request without automatic history replay. Results are withheld until acknowledgment; after delivery they cannot be recalled.

  • Preserve and refuse (no inference): an earlier message was edited (prefix_diverged), the history had an unexpected tail (unexpected_tail), a forced tool choice arrived (forced_choice), an effort change arrived while tools were pending (effort_midturn). Gateway keeps the existing CLI, ledger and pending relay calls intact and returns a final HTTP 400 (invalid_prompt in Responses streams). It neither sends the rejected input nor falls back to one-shot replay. A corrected request can continue the same session; edited history requires client compaction through Gateway, a new compaction window, or a fresh chat. Old replay holds for these mismatch reasons also refuse further replay after an in-place upgrade.

  • Native Messages history replacement: an identified Claude Code session without a thread header owns its full history. Native /compact can edit an earlier message and remove the latest answer without a compaction/window marker. Once the CLI has finished and no tools are pending, a changed prefix therefore uses one cache-budgeted replacement (client_history_replaced). Gateway does not infer compaction from prompt text or grant a separate compaction budget for that unmarked request. With hint headers on, the summary request is marked as compaction and takes the compaction path instead. Pending tool mismatches still preserve and refuse. Explicit thread IDs retain the preservation behavior above.

  • Dead session: a crashed CLI cannot be preserved. Its existing replay hold remains bounded by the shared cache guard and expires after an idle hour. Each ordinary retry restarts that hour. Explicit client compaction can recover the same chat: only a successful, uncancelled compaction clears the unchanged crash hold. A newer session or replacement hold remains protected. Gateway does not replay the failed request automatically.

  • Cancellation timeout: if a cancelled turn does not produce its interrupt result within two seconds, Gateway deliberately closes that CLI. This is a controlled cancellation, so it creates no crash hold. The cancelled request stays cancelled; only a later caller request can start a new session, under the existing cache guard. Genuine CLI crashes still retain their replay holds. Existing holds are not retroactively cleared, and sessions retained across an in-place upgrade keep the cancellation behavior of the code that created them.

  • Refused turn: a reasoning_extraction refusal ends the session (closed, reason refused) without a hold, so the next message starts a new session and reaches Claude. Rebuilding the chat costs one full resend, and the cache stop limits repeats. A CLI that exits during a turn gets up to 250 ms for its last lines to be read, so a refusal printed just before the exit is not recorded as a crash.

  • Rejected tool name: an unknown tool, unavailable gateway tool or forbidden native helper stops the response before any tool from that response is forwarded. Gateway deliberately kills that CLI for confinement, records closed rather than crashed, and does not create an hour-long crash hold. The failed request remains final. Only a new caller request can start a replacement under the existing cache guard. No tool is guessed, executed, remapped or automatically retried. Adopted older sessions get the same hold release only when their own request reports one of these fixed tool-name rejections; unrelated crash holds remain protected. A hold created before this fix is not cleared retroactively.

  • Capacity (no eviction): see Admission below.

  • Warmup (no session): a thread must complete warmup ordinary requests before its first live CLI starts. Until then, it runs one-shot with the warmup miss reason. This keeps composer prediction forks and one-request subagents from occupying a parked CLI for an hour. With the default policy, identified histories of at least 256 KiB of serialized conversation skip the one-shot warmup and seed live directly. This avoids two large cache writes before the first native continuation after a restart or cache expiry. Explicit warmup settings remain authoritative; this does not raise the two-miss safety budget. For small requests, the default of one is cheap: the promoted session seed reads the cache the one-shot request wrote and writes only its new content.

  • Standalone requests: explicitly identified compaction, prewarm, memory and Claude Code side requests, first questions without a conversation ID, and configured warmup. Codex's explicit thread_source: "composer_predictions" and "thread_sample" metadata also select standalone execution. These requests belong to temporary threads that the client destroys after sampling; even a large inherited history must not leave a parked CLI or consume a live-session slot. Their ordinary cache safety budget still applies. Other thread sources keep normal live continuity. Anonymous historical conversations require an ID instead of repeated replay.

  • Continuity refusal: capacity, concurrent requests, failed startup or an unavailable live adapter stop before one-shot replay. The CLI and its tool server have 60 seconds to start (initialize_timeout); a loaded Mac took up to 25 seconds, so the earlier 15-second limit refused live chats. CLI failure remains final after partial output too. A failed forced-tool choice never retries with a changed catalog. See provider reuse.

Bounded cache rewrites

The shared cache guard applies to every provider and ingress protocol. The Claude adapter also retains native input measurements on failures. A replacement seed checks the cache budget and cancellation before retiring the old session. A refused replacement leaves the live process and pending tools intact. Between-turn effort changes check that budget before sending a control update. Normal model, tools, system instructions, compaction-window changes and idle expiry still require a controlled reseed; the gateway never pretends incompatible history can continue unchanged. Process crashes, unsafe native tools, shutdown and expired park timers still close sessions. This does not preserve a CLI across a full inference-process restart. A completed compaction through Gateway permits one replacement history even when the client does not send a window ID. Failed or cancelled compaction grants no replacement, and completion cannot authorize resetting a concurrently replaced session.

Two consecutive measured requests that each write at least 65,536 cache tokens and write more than they read stop the next request before inference. This applies to live continuations as well as new seeds and one-shot replay. The client receives a final HTTP 400 explaining the cache problem, rather than a retryable stream disconnect. context_cache_guard records only a hashed key, mode and count and appears in recent diagnostics.

A measured small write or majority cache read clears the streak. Missing cache counts do not count as recovery. Client compaction requests have a separate bounded budget; a replacement conversation input at most half the byte size of the failed history can recover on the same model. The gateway does not compact, truncate history, change models or execute tools. Reading at least 75% of the preceding request's cached prefix also clears the streak: a large new tool result must not be mistaken for repeatedly rewriting old history. Measured input-cache counts also survive a later stream failure, rejected tool or cancellation. Missing counts remain unknown and do not erase a previous failure.

The bounded safety state is account-, model- and caller-scoped and survives client reconnects and in-place upgrades. It retains at most 4,096 entries in the inference process. Anonymous requests share their account/model budget. A full inference-process restart resets it. Repeated large inputs with unreported cache usage stop with a distinct explanation rather than being treated as measured zero cache reuse.

Reasoning-summary replay

The Claude route preserves readable reasoning summaries as typed metadata at the Responses restoration boundary. Text replay gives them a reasoning_summary item header; JSON replay retains reasoningSummary: true. Their text stays unchanged. Ordinary assistant messages remain ordinary assistant messages, including valid string-content messages. The session ledger skips typed reasoning metadata while counting the messages the renderer emits, so a genuine assistant answer cannot disappear from history matching because of its string encoding. Other providers retain their previous restoration behavior, including account-scoped Codex encrypted-state round trips.

A public summary has no native Claude thinking signature. The gateway never fabricates one or reconstructs an unsigned thinking block from the summary. The caller's instructions, saved chat ID, archive, answers, calls and tool outputs remain intact. A replay-contract revision makes an adopted idle session reseed once through the existing fingerprint-change path. Requests already in flight finish on their original runtime.

This corrects a representation error; it does not establish which passage a provider classifier rejected or override a provider refusal.

Admission

A session is evicted only after it has been idle for 60 minutes, the length of the 1 h cache. While every slot holds a warm session, a new thread is refused (capacity) until a slot frees; nothing is evicted and no warm cache is spent on a newcomer. Sessions being started count toward max, in arrival order, so concurrent attaches can never run more processes than the cap. Telemetry records the warmup standalone requests and refused capacity/replay-hold reasons as claude_session events with fallback or blocked and the thread's threadKey. A promoted spawn has afterWarmup: true, so diagnostics records its cache cost; see diagnostics.

The limit is shared across Claude accounts in one inference process; it is not an Anthropic quota or the number of currently running turns. A finished turn keeps its parked slot until expiry. Increasing max applies on configuration reload without closing existing sessions. Set the same value on each Claude provider because the provider admitting a new session applies its setting to the shared pool. There is no fixed ceiling for an explicit value. Each additional session consumes local memory; the memory-derived default remains conservative.

The system prompt is the gateway's fixed text plus the caller's instructions and the system and developer messages before the first other message, as on the one-shot path (see Responses support). It lives in a private file in the session directory. Those messages are not part of the session's history ledger; the session fingerprint covers them, so a change to them reseeds. A later developer message is history and continues the session like any other new item.

An effort change between turns uses the CLI's apply_flag_settings and keeps the cache. Cancelling interrupts the turn and keeps the session; the next history may keep or drop the partial text. The session closes instead if a tool call was being written.

Prompt cache across threads

Each Claude request's system array has a billing header with no cache marker, then the CLI identity block with a breakpoint, then one block with a breakpoint that joins the gateway's fixed text to the caller's leading system and developer content. --append-system-prompt-file joins that same block and creates no separate breakpoint. --exclude-dynamic-system-prompt-sections is ignored with a custom system prompt. The CLI sorts tools alphabetically and marks no tool.

Gateway also canonicalizes the caller tool catalog by native name and sorts schema object keys without changing array order or values. Harmless catalog reordering therefore keeps the same fingerprint. Existing adopted sessions with an older fingerprint may need one controlled replacement.

A new thread therefore reuses the tools, billing header and identity block from another thread's cache. It reuses caller instructions only when they are byte-identical, such as two root chats within the cache lifetime. On 2026-10-19, a new thread's first request read 33,331 cached tokens 66 seconds after another thread on the same model. A subagent, or any thread whose leading instructions differ, rewrites that block. The gateway does not move caller developer text into user history to improve this cache reuse because that would change its role.

The block layout was captured with CLI 2.1.299 in API-key mode against a local mock. The subscription cache TTL is one hour: a direct CLI run reported ephemeral_1h_input_tokens of 9,604 and ephemeral_5m_input_tokens of 0.

Safety

The live CLI sees only the gateway's MCP tools: it runs with --tools "", --allowedTools limited to the gateway, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_ADVISOR_TOOL=1 and ENABLE_TOOL_SEARCH=false, as one-shot CLIs now do too. A tool_use for anything else kills the session as soon as the gateway reads that line, and the request fails with invalid_tool_call. No gateway CLI inherits the host's CLAUDECODE, CLAUDE_CODE_* or CLAUDE_AGENT_SDK_* variables; the gateway sets its own, including CLAUDE_CODE_MAX_MCP_DESCRIPTION_LENGTH, so caller tool descriptions are not cut. Nothing is written to ~/.claude: sessions use --no-session-persistence and a private working directory inside its own generation under $TMPDIR/gateway-claude-v2. Closing a session removes only that generation, including its working directory. The next process start sweeps generations whose gateway owner has died. New generations sit outside the legacy per-thread tree, so cleanup by a session adopted from an older release cannot delete a replacement's files. Live sessions set DISABLE_AUTO_COMPACT=1; Codex owns compaction. Legacy per-thread working directories remain when sweeping old storage, because an older process may still be starting a session there.

Request rejections

Claude invalid_request failures are final HTTP 400 errors. Responses streams use invalid_prompt, so the desktop stops retrying an unchanged rejected request. A recognized credit refusal still takes billing precedence, and context overflow still permits the caller's normal compaction recovery. The native reasoning_extraction refusal gets a fixed explanation of Claude's protection policy; the gateway preserves caller history, instructions and model choice. The refusal does not hold the chat, so a person can send another message. See request rejection diagnostics.

Authentication failures

The CLI's authentication_failed code does not by itself prove that the user must sign in again. The gateway classifies bounded diagnostics from native failure envelopes into fixed reasons: login_unavailable, session_expired, credential_revoked, upstream_rejected, or unknown. It never saves the diagnostic text. Local claude auth status reports credential presence; it does not prove that an inference request will authenticate. An unclassified failure therefore suggests retrying and signing in if it persists, rather than asserting that the saved login has expired.

An explicit generic upstream HTTP 401, identified by the CLI's native error prefix, gets one fresh one-shot attempt after a cancellable two-second wait. This recovery is allowed only before any inference event has reached the caller. The same model, instructions, history and tools are used, and a failed live session closes before the replacement starts. Text, reasoning or a dispatched tool makes the failure final for this request. Missing, expired, revoked and unclassified logins also remain final, as do billing and subscription limits. A second failure preserves its original error. Recovery never resumes a stopped goal, answers an approval, or replays an executed command.

A native authentication failure before any inference output, tool-result delivery or queued steering closes the live session without a crash hold. A later caller request can therefore try the saved login again, including after the bounded upstream-401 recovery succeeds. The failed request remains final when it is not eligible for that existing recovery. Authentication failures after output or a tool handoff retain the crash hold because the turn may have advanced. The cache guard still checks any replacement history. When the CLI exits with an unread authentication frame, the first queued terminal frame supplies the failure and the same safety boundary applies. An earlier successful result or another failure cannot be replaced by a later authentication diagnostic. Sessions adopted from an older release remain conservative; an existing crash hold is not retroactively cleared.

On October 21, 2026, five fresh one-shot requests failed with authentication_failed between 10:33 and 10:36 Europe/Belgrade, each before any inference event. Two original chats later continued without a recorded login change. Earlier telemetry did not retain a failure reason, so it cannot prove whether those failures involved credential access, expiry or upstream rejection. The guarded recovery addresses the explicit upstream-401 shape; it is not a demonstrated reproduction of that incident.

Context management

The CLI sends only clear_thinking with keep: all, which removes nothing. Version 2.1.293 also contains clear_tool_uses, behind a server flag that is off by default. It applies only to a conversation that returns after at least 65 minutes idle with at least 20 tool uses. A session idle 60 minutes or more is therefore reseeded rather than continued, so Claude's history always matches what Codex sent.

Measured

The isolated scripts/e2e-claude-sampling.mjs check uses a real app-server SDK and synthetic Claude CLI replies. With a one-slot pool already held by the parent chat, three thread/sample composer predictions must each finish without parking another CLI, then the parent must continue on its original session. Run it after building, with --sdk /absolute/sdk --catalog /absolute/models_cache.json --root /tmp/fresh-sampling-proof. It uses private homes and no paid inference. Add --tool-recovery to also prove that a native turn rejected for an unknown tool fails once without replay, then a separate caller message succeeds in the same chat without an hour-long hold. Use --legacy-package /absolute/older-release/package with that option to start the session on an older implementation before adopting it into the candidate.

On 1 November 2026, native Claude Code 2.1.299 and the installed Codex app-server SDK each completed a three-request tool loop using one backend process through an isolated Gateway. Codex also resumed the saved chat and continued its next turn. Backend inference was synthetic, so this proves client and session continuity, not subscription cost parity or a guaranteed provider cache hit. An independent native CLI probe on 2.1.299 and 2.1.303 with a local mock Anthropic API confirmed the queued-input ordering barrier with two inference requests and about 17 ms of control overhead. The barrier runs only when caller messages follow pending tool results. The same native client also completed /compact and continued two subsequent turns against the candidate with synthetic backend replies: five requests used three backend processes. The summary request replaced history once; the changed native system attribution after compaction required another replacement. Ordinary follow-ups continued. This establishes compatibility, not cost-free compaction.

Haiku 5.5 and Sonnet 5.5, CLI 2.1.293:

  • A continued request reads the whole cached prefix and writes only its new content (74–108 tokens on a tool loop), with 2 uncached input tokens. A one-shot request reads the previous request's prefix and writes its new items plus about 350 tokens of the CLI's trailing reminder, as long as every block ends in a non-space character (see the closing line in responses).
  • A session's second user turn misses 350–430 tokens once, whatever the seed size. The seed itself is not rewritten. A turn that ends in tool use has no such miss.
  • Each session uses about 240 MB for the CLI and 44 MB for its MCP child, which is why the default pool is sized at 300 MB a slot.
  • On 2026-10-19, CLI 2.1.299 with Haiku 5.5, a subscription login, an approximately 8k-token fixed instruction prefix and synthetic history served a first one-shot request with 0 cache-read tokens and 21,319 cache-write tokens. Its second request, which spawned after warmup, read 20,960 and wrote 423, so the session seed read the one-shot cache instead of rewriting it. The next continued turn read 21,016 and wrote 435. Changing effort from low to medium continued through apply_flag_settings and read 21,426 while writing 95. A control new thread with different history read only the shared system prefix (12,159) and wrote 9,167.
  • Before the admission policy, least-recently-used eviction on a working set larger than the pool evicted the thread needed next. One window with 7 threads against max 6 saw 14 evictions after a median 49 s idle (20–160 s, against a 1 h cache), and every evicted thread came back. Its 22 reseeds read 0.686M tokens (only the shared system prefix) and wrote 1.496M, against 0.804M for spawns and 0.241M for continues: reseeds were 59% of all cache writes. Concurrent starts bypassed the cap, so 7 sessions ran at max 6.
  • A text turn's result arrives 3–7 ms after its final message_delta, so a live request still ends at the result. One-shot requests end at that delta instead, except Fast ones, which need the result's fast mode state.

Restarts and upgrades

An in-place upgrade keeps the sessions: the registry lives on a versioned global symbol, so the new runtime adopts the one it finds and adds the collections a later release introduced (replayUntil, scopes) to it in place. An adopted session is still its thread's session: the next request continues the running process and records its provider scope as it goes. A registry reporting another interface version is not adopted but replaced, and its sessions are left to their own park timers. An inference restart reseeds each active thread once. The release that moved caller instructions into the system prompt changes every session's fingerprint, so each thread reseeds once after it even when an in-place upgrade adopted its session; that reseed is the chat's one cache write. On shutdown, idle sessions close at once and a running turn closes when it ends; the relay's dead-man check and stdin EOF stop any CLI whose gateway died. claude_session telemetry records each outcome; see diagnostics.
